problems.quote: the Currency Ordinance of 1940 replaced the silver rupee with a managed paper currency
problems.problem: The Currency Ordinance 1940 did not replace the silver rupee; it authorized the issue of Government of India one‑rupee notes. The silver rupee had already ceased to be the monetary standard.
problems.correction: the Currency Ordinance of 1940 authorized the issue of one‑rupee notes by the Government of India
problems.verifierReason: Currency Ordinance 1940 authorized Govt 1-rupee notes; silver rupee had ceased as standard earlier.

problems.quote: The intermediate aggregates M1 and M2 are constructed by progressively adding savings deposits and short‑term time deposits, respectively
problems.problem: M1 does not include savings deposits; M2 adds savings deposits to M1, and M3 adds time deposits. The description misstates the composition of M1 and M2.
problems.correction: M2 adds savings deposits to M1, and M3 adds time deposits to M2
problems.verifierReason: Indian M1 excludes savings deposits; M2 adds savings deposits, M3 adds time deposits.

problems.quote: uses them as intermediate targets when the operating framework shifts from a monetary targeting regime to the current flexible inflation targeting framework
problems.problem: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework, monetary aggregates are not used as intermediate targets; the policy repo rate is the operating target.
problems.correction: monitors them as indicators under the flexible inflation targeting framework
problems.verifierReason: Under flexible inflation targeting (since 2016), monetary aggregates are indicators, not intermediate targets.

problems.quote: typically monthly for EBLR and quarterly for MCLR
problems.problem: The reset frequency is monthly for MCLR and quarterly for EBLR; the statement reverses them.
problems.correction: typically monthly for MCLR and quarterly for EBLR
problems.verifierReason: MCLR reset is monthly; EBLR reset is quarterly per RBI guidelines.

problems.quote: in 2011 the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) was added, allowing banks to borrow overnight up to 2 per cent of their net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) at a rate 25 basis points above the repo rat
problems.problem: When introduced in 2011, the MSF limit was 1% of NDTL and the rate was 100 bps above the repo rate. The 2% limit and 25 bps spread were adopted later.
problems.correction: in 2011 the MSF was added, allowing banks to borrow up to 1% of NDTL at 100 bps above repo; the limit was later raised to 2% and the spread reduced to 25 bps
problems.verifierReason: MSF introduced 2011 at 1% NDTL, 100bps above repo; limit later 2%, spread 25bps.
